core_requests: P075 c1: render the provider UA placeholder {app} from a setting (e.g. phishtank_app_name = the team's own registered PhishTank username/app name, default 'v3lum') instead of the constant 'v3lum' (v3lum/core/http.py _render_template); modules may not set a UA themselves

P075 c5: a read-only view of the run entity's case-graph tags in ctx (e.g. ctx.entity_tags) so phishtank_checkurl can accept pivots tagged phishing/suspicious; today it accepts analyst-typed seeds and provenance relation listed_phishing_url only

P075 c5 / P073 c2: feed provider-announced limits from response headers (PhishTank X-Request-Limit/-Interval/-Count, BuiltWith X-API-CREDITS-REMAINING / X-RATELIMIT-*) into the P334 quota book; the modules keep a local window/credit budget in ctx.state meanwhile
P069 c5: a per-scan budget API (quota book reserve(scope='run') or similar) for module-level per-case query caps; public_api_exposure keeps a per-case counter in ctx.state meanwhile
P073 c5: accept UA account-level ids ('UA-123456', as BuiltWith reports them) in entities.normalize(ANALYTICS_ID), or document that they stay labels; today they cannot become analytics_id entities
P073 (A15/P379): a key self-test hook (HealthCheck selftest for keys) so builtwith can check the key with the no-credit whoamiv1 call

cross-batch (not core): the phishtank provider fragment owned by p1-G03-1 should take tier 'trusted' (P075 chair), a quota block for the 250/300 s per-IP window and the env alias V3LUM_PHISHTANK_APPKEY; the builtwith seed should carry the team plan's day/credit figures in its quota block
notes: All three modules are PASSIVE, third_party, default_enabled=False; no LIGHT/ACTIVE variant is asked. public_api_exposure is one aggregator with two sources: postman.public_search (terms unknown -> POL-04 keeps it out of ctx.allowed_sources under every licence profile; manual link public_api_exposure:postman_search) and apisguru.directory (CC0, open; the 8.9 MB list.json is a large dataset matched locally, never downloaded by a lookup; POL-14 gives UNAVAILABLE dataset until `v3lum data update public_api_exposure.apisguru_list`). Postman queries only org_profile domains/brands, one query per entity, 2 pages, 6 per case, 50/day provider budget; hits kept only on request-host or publisher ties; request URLs shown with every query value masked and secret types only (key renamed exposed_kinds because the sanitizer masks values under 'secret' keys); Postman answers are never cached. builtwith: free mode (free1) by default, domain mode (v21 + rv5 page 1) by setting builtwith_mode; NOPII=yes and HIDETEXT=yes on every call; KEY= in the URL masked by the central redactor (AR01); Errors[] markers added in builtwith__p3-G03-1.json (-3 credits -> QUOTA, deliberately the contract-v2 budget status instead of FC4's RATE_LIMITED so the quota book stops paid lookups; -7 -> RATE_LIMITED); -2/-5 -> NEEDS_KEY and the rest ERROR in the module; P061 shared-id, pivot-cap, overlap and clone rules applied (possible-clone findings never tag the own site hostile). P073 c6 (merge only with a real team-key success fixture) cannot be met: success fixtures are BuiltWith's documented samples, recorded in the backlog. phishtank_checkurl: checkurl.phishtank.com is mapped to no provider in owners.json but the provider id derived from the domain (phishtank) exists (p1-G03-1), so it is extended (phishtank__p3-G03-1.json: host, source phishtank.phishtank_checkurl, markers meta.status error -> ERROR and HTTP 509 -> RATE_LIMITED; phishtank.org/www.phishtank.com registered for the manual links). The UA is the core-bound profile 'phishtank/{app}' -> 'phishtank/v3lum' (see core_requests for the setting). The derived trust tier is community because the existing provider says so (council: trusted). Block streak and per-IP window live in ctx.state; after 5 consecutive BLOCKED runs automatic runs are link-only (SKIPPED demoted). Prep parsers (code/parsers.py) were ported and adapted to contract v2; fixtures re-checked (documentation values only, PhishTank request ids redacted). P327 lint, ruff and the registry contract test are clean for the batch files.
